title: Centered linear-square moment bound
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $f$ be a function from the sign cube $\\{-1,1\\}^n$ to $\\{-1,1\\}$. For each subset $S\\subseteq\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$, let $\\widehat f(S)$ be its Fourier coefficient, and let $W_1(f)=\\sum_{|S|=1}\\widehat f(S)^2$. If $0\\le\\delta\\le 1/1600$ and $W_1(f)=1-\\delta$, then, for a uniformly random $x\\in\\{-1,1\\}^n$, the expected square of $\\bigl(\\sum_{i=1}^n\\widehat f(\\{i\\})x_i\\bigr)^2-\\sum_{i=1}^n\\widehat f(\\{i\\})^2$ is at most $6400\\delta$.
hypotheses_covered: the level-one Fourier weight of $f$ equals $1-\\delta$
